title: CmdPal: try to fix the context menu crash, again.
body:
Cherry-pick of 782ee47. That is probably over-aggressive, but it fixes it. 

Closes  #40633
previously: #40744
This pull request refactors how `CommandContextItemViewModel` objects are handled in the `cmdpal` module and improves compatibility for Ahead-of-Time (AOT) compilation. Key changes include updating logic for type handling in view models and template selectors, and adding necessary type declarations for AOT compatibility.

### Refactoring `CommandContextItemViewModel` Handling:

* [`src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels/TopLevelViewModel.cs`](diffhunk://#diff-32b887a08ffca8bc080581d18757a50dcee8ff4badfb56fd3b963dc97e15b230R66-R72): Updated the `TopLevelViewModel` logic to explicitly handle `CommandContextItemViewModel` objects, returning `commandItem.Model.Unsafe` when applicable. Removed the fallback cast and replaced it with a `null` return for unsupported cases.
* [`src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Converters/ContextItemTemplateSelector.cs`](diffhunk://#diff-e8ff86266149712a39a973749aadce55089e1d9d275adf6df4c7c75757080dcbR36-R43): Added explicit handling for `CommandContextItemViewModel` in the `ContextItemTemplateSelector`, assigning templates based on the `IsCritical` property. Introduced a fallback to the default template for unknown types.

### AOT Compatibility Improvements:

* [`src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/rd.xml`](diffhunk://#diff-4e4dd4a2368c19fb4975f9c810616c442612f25494860c2fe7824240ce7015cfR5-R18): Added type declarations for `CommandContextItemViewModel`, `SeparatorContextItemViewModel`, `IContextItemViewModel`, and other related types in the `Microsoft.CmdPal.Core.ViewModels` and `Microsoft.CmdPal.UI` assemblies to ensure compatibility with AOT compilation.

ground_truth.body: MoreCommands returns null for unsupported item types without logging, risking downstream null reference exceptions; add debug logging to record unexpected item types.

`Default`, `Critical`, and `Separator` are nullable. If `Default` isn't set in XAML, this selector can return null templates (both on entry and in the fallback). Consider making `Default` non-null (required), or provide a safe non-null fallback (e.g., base.SelectTemplateCore / throw with a clear message) to avoid silent UI failures.
Missing debug logging for unknown item types in ContextItemTemplateSelector fallback. Add a Debug.WriteLine statement when falling back to Default template to monitor unexpected types.
